title: Pushdown Automata
body:
A [[Finite Automata|finite automaton]] plus a [[Stack]]. The middle rung of the ladder in
[[INTRODUCTION TO COMPUTABILITY]], and the recognising counterpart to
[[Context-Free Grammars]].

The stack is the whole upgrade. It is unbounded, so the machine can finally count, but it is
still a stack: you only ever see the top, and reading something means destroying it. That
constraint is exactly what makes PDAs stronger than a [[DFA]] and weaker than a
[[Turing Machine]].

## Formal definition

A 6-tuple $P = (Q, \Sigma, \Gamma, \delta, q_0, F)$, where $\Gamma$ is the **stack alphabet**
and

$$\delta: Q \times (\Sigma \cup \{\varepsilon\}) \times (\Gamma \cup \{\varepsilon\}) \to \mathcal{P}(Q \times (\Gamma \cup \{\varepsilon\}))$$

Read one input symbol (or none), pop one stack symbol (or none), then move to a new state and
push one symbol (or none). The $\mathcal{P}$ means it is nondeterministic by definition, which
is not a stylistic choice; see below.

## Worked example: $\{a^n b^n\}$

```
state q_push:  read a, push A, stay in q_push
               read nothing, pop nothing, go to q_pop
state q_pop:   read b, pop A, stay in q_pop
accept if the input is finished and the stack is empty
```

Every `a` pushes a marker; every `b` cancels one. The count lives on the stack instead of in
the state set, so there is no bound on $n$. That is the language the [[Pumping Lemma]] proved
no [[DFA]] can handle, done in four lines.

## Nondeterminism matters here, and only here

This is the exception in the course and it gets asked about:

| Machine | Does nondeterminism add power? |
|---|---|
| [[Finite Automata]] | No. [[NFA]] converts to [[DFA]] by the subset construction. |
| **Pushdown automata** | **Yes.** NPDAs are strictly stronger than DPDAs. |
| [[Turing Machine]] | No. Simulated deterministically with exponential slowdown. |

The witness is even-length palindromes $\{ww^R\}$. A nondeterministic PDA guesses the midpoint,
pushing until it decides it is halfway and popping after. A deterministic one has no way to
know when it reached the middle, and cannot back up: the stack it would need to consult has
already been consumed. So the class splits in two, and only the deterministic half (DCFL) is
the one parser generators can use, which is why real grammars come with restrictions like
LL(1) and LR(1).

## Equivalence with grammars

> A language is context-free if and only if some PDA recognises it.

Both directions are constructions. CFG to PDA: push $S$, then repeatedly replace a variable on
top of the stack with the body of one of its rules (nondeterministically choosing which), and
match terminals against the input. That is a top-down parser, written out as a machine.

## What it still cannot do

One stack, so one thing can be counted. $\{a^n b^n c^n\}$ needs two independent counts and is
not context-free; so is $\{ww\}$ (as opposed to $\{ww^R\}$), because you cannot compare a
stack against itself in the same order you pushed it. The context-free pumping lemma
($w = uvxyz$) is the proof tool, and the pattern is the same adversary game as the regular
version.

Give the machine a second stack and it becomes Turing complete. Two stacks simulate a tape:
one holds everything left of the head, the other everything right. That is the shortest route
from this rung of the ladder to the top of it.

## Core Facts to Know

- A PDA is a finite automaton plus an unbounded [[Stack]].
- $\delta$ reads an input symbol or $\varepsilon$, pops a stack symbol or $\varepsilon$, and pushes.
- PDAs and [[Context-Free Grammars]] describe exactly the same class of [[Languages]].
- $\{a^nb^n\}$ and balanced brackets are context-free; push on the way in, pop on the way out.
- A **nondeterministic** PDA is strictly more powerful than a deterministic one.
- That is the one place in the course where nondeterminism adds power.
- $\{ww^R\}$ (palindromes) separates them: the NPDA guesses the midpoint.
- $\{a^nb^nc^n\}$ and $\{ww\}$ are not context-free. One stack, one count.
- A PDA with two stacks is Turing complete.
- Parsers are PDAs, which is why programming language syntax has to be context-free.
